IT Systems Administrator MIT Lincoln Laboratory is seeking an early-career IT Systems Administrator to join a technical team supporting secure, mission-focused research and development environments. The selected candidate will help deploy, operate, maintain, and secure Windows- and Linux-based information systems and supporting infrastructure. This role is well suited to an individual with a strong foundation in desktop support, systems administration, networking, and cybersecurity who is interested in growing into an independent systems administrator within a complex and highly regulated environment. Job Description The IT Systems Administrator will help provide reliable, secure, and responsive computing services for Group 96 personnel, laboratory environments, and program infrastructure. The position will support the deployment, operation, maintenance, and security of Windows- and Linux-based systems used for engineering, development, test, analysis, and administrative activities. This role requires close coordination with Group 96 technical staff, Information Services Department personnel, cybersecurity personnel, network engineers, information system security officers, and program stakeholders. The successful candidate will support a mix of enterprise IT services, specialized program systems, laboratory equipment, and systems operating in restricted, disconnected, or classified environments. Group 96’s work requires strong attention to operational reliability, configuration control, cybersecurity compliance, documentation, and timely technical support. The selected candidate will assist with maintaining secure system baselines; supporting endpoint, server, and virtual infrastructure; managing user access; resolving technical issues; and preparing systems for security reviews, assessments, and mission needs. The position offers an opportunity to develop expertise in: Secure Windows and Linux systems administration Administration of systems supporting research, development, integration, and test activities Configuration management and controlled system deployment Virtualization, storage, backup, and recovery technologies Identity, access, and privilege management Cybersecurity hardening, vulnerability remediation, and STIG compliance Support for disconnected, restricted-network, and classified computing environments Collaboration with engineers, developers, technical program staff, and cybersecurity professionals The IT Systems Administrator will be expected to work under the guidance of senior systems administrators while progressively assuming responsibility for independently managing assigned systems, resolving technical issues, documenting configurations and procedures, and contributing to Group 96 infrastructure-improvement initiatives. Assist with administration and maintenance of Linux systems, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux and Ubuntu environments. Diagnose and resolve hardware, software, operating system, and network-connectivity issues. Monitor system availability, performance, event logs, and operational health. Support patch management, software updates, endpoint maintenance, and vulnerability remediation activities. Assist with backup, restoration, and data-recovery procedures. Maintain accurate hardware inventories, configuration-management records, technical documentation, and standard operating procedures. Support physical and virtual server infrastructure, including VMware or comparable virtualization technologies. Assist with basic network troubleshooting involving TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VLANs, firewall connectivity, and network file shares. Support systems in disconnected, restricted-network, or classified computing environments as required by program assignments. Apply and validate secure system configurations in accordance with Laboratory policy, customer requirements, and applicable cybersecurity guidance. Assist with system hardening, Security Technical Implementation Guide implementation, vulnerability scanning, remediation tracking, and continuous-monitoring activities. Work closely with information system security personnel to identify, document, and remediate system configuration deficiencies. Document incidents, system changes, maintenance activities, and technical resolutions. Participate in technology-refresh, infrastructure-improvement, and process-improvement initiatives. Escalate complex technical issues appropriately while maintaining ownership of assigned tasks through resolution. Education Requirements Bachelor’s degree in information technology, computer science, information systems, cybersecurity, engineering, or a related technical field; or an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience. Required Qualifications One or more years of relevant experience in IT technical support, desktop support, systems administration, or a comparable technical role. Experience troubleshooting Windows operating systems, hardware, software, and network connectivity. Familiarity with Microsoft Active Directory and user-account administration. Strong analytical, troubleshooting, organizational, and customer-service skills. Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary technical team. Preferred Skills Experience supporting Windows Server, including Windows Server 2019, 2022, or later versions. Experience supporting Windows 10 or Windows 11 Enterprise environments. Exposure to Linux administration, particularly Red Hat Enterprise Linux or Ubuntu. Experience with VMware vSphere, ESXi, or comparable virtualization platforms. Familiarity with Group Policy, Windows Server Update Services, endpoint-management platforms, or software-deployment tools. Familiarity with DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides, NIST security controls, or cybersecurity compliance processes. Experience supporting Department of Defense, U.S. Government, research, or similarly regulated computing environments. Experience with PowerShell, Bash, Python, or other scripting and automation tools. Familiarity with enterprise monitoring, vulnerability-management, antivirus, endpoint-detection, or endpoint-protection tools. Experience with backup, restoration, and disaster-recovery technologies. Understanding of public-key infrastructure, certificates, multifactor authentication, and identity-management concepts. The role is hands-on general system administration, at the intermediate to senior level. Its core is Microsoft Azure, Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft 365. You will also work on systems, endpoints, networks and user needs, without being limited to one specialty. You will own your work, from daily operations to project delivery. Work on a modern Microsoft cloud stack, including the move to Intune, Windows Autopilot and Global Secure Access. Use approved AI tools in your daily technical work. Unification: bring the different entities and sites under a common Corporate IT operating model and reduce dependence on local or undocumented practices. Automation: replace repetitive manual work with scripts, APIs and built-in platform automation. Securisation: strengthen identity, access, endpoint and network security, including MFA, least privilege, endpoint protection and patching.
